newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Maersk-owned Estonian Air sees better 1996 sales.
newsitem.headline: Maersk-owned Estonian Air sees better 1996 sales.

text.p: National carrier Estonian Air, part of the Maersk Air group, said on Wednesday that its 1996 turnover was 365 million kroons, an improvement from the 309 million kroons registered in 1995.
The company, which is 66 percent owned by Maersk, itself part of the A.P. Moeller combine, and local investment group Baltic Cresco, forecast turnover of 509 million kroons for 1997.
"Based on first quarter results we are on target for the 500 million figure," Borge Thornbech, president of Estonian Air, told journalists.
Thornbech declined to say what the company's first quarter results were.
"Our first quarter figures are in line with our budget predictions," he added.
The company did not make a proft in 1996 and is not expected to bring a profit until the year 1999.
"We will make a loss this year and next year, and we predict that will make a profit in 1999," Thornbech said.
"This is a normal situation in turning a company around," he said.
Estonian Air was privatised in 1996 and has been pursuing a moderisation programme.
The government retains a 34 percent stake in the company with Maersh Air holding 49 percent and Baltic Cresco the remaining 17 percent.
Maersk joined rival airline Scandinavian Airlines in the Baltic market as SAS owns around a third of Latvia's national airline, Air Baltic.
